paragraphs: Self-questioning | Are you willing to listen to illness-related social and family difficulties, verify resource conditions, coordinate handovers, and record truthfully? This checklist is not an ability score or hiring standard. Start by using the fictional paper materials of H01 to experience record-keeping and referral preparation, without touching real medical records or service recipients.

Exercise prompt | A completely fictional healthcare psychosocial support and case management task package (for practice workflow only; it does not represent any real institution, service recipient, family, or data). Write a draft plan: (1) how, based on a fictional referral form along with a medical record summary and psychosocial assessment key points, to arrange a case in a structured way (service recipient and family circumstances, needs and risk identification, accessible resources and referral list, care and intervention goals and plan, crisis contingency and safety plan, confidentiality and consent and information disclosure boundaries, records and review, and evaluation and case closure), and state which information is insufficient and needs to be supplemented (disease diagnosis and prognosis and treatment plan, family caregiving resources and financial situation, needs such as housing and legal aid and employment, substance misuse and mental health and safety risks, language and cultural differences, and consent capacity and ethics and confidentiality exception requirements); (2) how to design the completion and review points for a fictional case record and progress and referral and cost record table (fields and definitions, service recipients and families, assessment and goals and intervention, progress and referrals and outcomes, exceptions and review and corrections, and original records and revision audit trails); (3) how to write a handover-ready case summary (service recipient—needs and basis—intervention and referrals—crisis and safety—confidentiality and consent—evaluation and case closure—open items); (4) how to record and preserve case and health and family information, and distinguish disclosable information from controlled materials or materials involving service recipients' and families' sensitive information; (5) how to pause, review, and escalate upon finding safety risks or suspected abuse or neglect or a confidentiality exception or exceeding the position's authorization. Answer using public materials and simulated data; do not use any real service recipient or family data.

Fit signals | The work activity importance scores for U.S. O*NET 21-1022.00 show that Assisting and Caring for Others (93), Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships (88), Getting Information (87), Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates (86), Communicating with People Outside the Organization (83), Documenting/Recording Information (83), Making Decisions and Solving Problems (81), Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others (81), Organizing, Planning, and Prioritizing Work (79), and Performing for or Working Directly with the Public (76) are the most important activities for this occupation; the work context (percentage response scope) shows telephone conversations 100% every day, face-to-face discussions 96% every day, electronic mail 93% every day, contact with others 85%, indoors, environmentally controlled 93% every day, work with a work group or team 73% extremely important, decision freedom 41% a lot of freedom, dealing with external customers or the public 44% extremely important, exposure to disease or infections 41% every day, conflict situations 19% every day and 59% once a week or more, consequence of error 11% extremely serious and 37% serious, and work schedule 96% regular. If you are willing to keep communicating with people in illness and crisis and their families, can make cases and records solid under multiple resource and institutional constraints, and are willing to take responsibility for service recipients' safety and privacy, the daily requirements of this occupation are closer to the way you work.

Caution signals | O*NET also shows (21-1022.00, work activity importance scope and work context percentage response scope): Assisting and Caring for Others (93), Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships (88), and Getting Information (87) are the highest activities; contact with others 85%, telephone conversations 100% every day, face-to-face discussions 96% every day, electronic mail 93% every day; exposure to disease or infections 41% every day and 30% once a week or more; time pressure 41% every day and 33% once a week or more; conflict situations 19% every day and 59% once a week or more; dealing with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people 22% every day and 52% once a week or more; facing violent or physically aggressive people 15% once a week or more and 22% once a month or more; consequence of error 11% extremely serious and 37% serious; working more than 40 hours per week 46%; responsibility for others' work outcomes 15% very high and 33% moderate; responsibility for others' health and safety 19% extremely high and 26% high. This occupation takes crisis intervention and case management and referral and recording as its subject matter, and a single improper crisis assessment or safety response, a single referral or resource linkage error, a single distorted case or progress or cost record, a single improper handling of a confidentiality exception or information disclosure, or a single out-of-bounds provision of clinical or psychological diagnosis and treatment advice can all harm service recipients' rights and safety and create institutional compliance and ethics risk. O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above); the education section of that page shows 70% master's degree, 15% bachelor's degree, and 11% post-master's certificate. If you find it hard to keep communicating with people in illness and trauma and crisis over the long term, hard to bear high conflict and emotional pressure, or unwilling to take responsibility for the truthfulness of privacy and confidentiality exceptions and ethics and records, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

Ownership judgment | Real fit comes from whether you can do three things at once on the same case and support task: do the profession properly (based on psychosocial assessment and care plans and accessible resources, complete needs and risk identification, intervention and referral and coordination, and progress monitoring and recording, and produce usable case and referral and progress and cost records), keep ethics and boundaries under control (work and keep an audit trail in line with confidentiality and informed consent and confidentiality exceptions and service recipient privacy and health information protection requirements; distinguish disclosable information from controlled materials or materials involving service recipients' and families' sensitive information and handle them according to policy; and do not overstep by providing clinical or psychological diagnosis and treatment advice or substituting for medical staff and judicial processes), and take on definable position responsibility (be accountable for the assessment and intervention and referral and records you personally perform, and refer matters beyond authorization or involving clinical judgment and diagnosis and treatment and placement and protection decisions and external disclosure to the appropriate position or institution according to policy). It is recommended to test this with one verifiable experience (completing a needs and resource assessment and a case and referral record note for a fictional case, or a retrospective review of handling one safety risk or confidentiality exception risk) rather than relying only on the conclusions of an interest questionnaire.

Direct answer | The "Healthcare Social Workers" on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 21-1022.00 (Healthcare Social Workers), and the work can be divided into several categories: first, crisis and advocacy — advocating for clients or patients to resolve crises (importance 94), and investigating child abuse or neglect cases and taking authorized protective action when necessary (88); second, assessment and care planning — collaborating with other professionals to assess patients' medical or physical condition and assess client needs (90), using consultation data and social work experience to plan and coordinate clients' or patients' care and rehabilitation and follow up to ensure services are effective (83), and modifying treatment plans as clients' conditions change (77); third, counseling and education — explaining terminal symptoms and available options to clients to help them make informed decisions (90), providing counseling to clients and patients individually and in groups to help them overcome dependencies and recover from illness and adjust to life (79), and organizing support groups or providing counseling to family members (77); fourth, referral and resource linkage — referring patients, clients, or families to community resources to assist their recovery and obtain services such as financial assistance and legal aid and housing and job placement or education (88), and identifying environmental barriers that impede clients' or patients' progress (81); fifth, monitoring and recording — monitoring, evaluating, and recording client progress against measurable goals in treatment and care plans (83), and overseeing Medicaid and Medicare related documentation and record work in hospitals (63); sixth, discharge and teams and programs — planning discharge arrangements for returning home from a care facility or to another care facility (77), supervising and guiding other staff who provide services to clients or patients (67), planning and conducting programs to address social problems, prevent substance misuse, or improve community health and counseling services (60), developing social policy recommendations or assisting community development (54), and conducting social research in the social work field to advance knowledge (50). Work cycle links: referral and needs and risk identification—psychosocial assessment and care planning—intervention and counseling and support—referral and resource linkage and coordination—progress monitoring and recording and review—discharge or case closure and handover and follow-up. This page does not conflate this occupation with adjacent ones such as mental health and substance abuse social workers, child and family and school social workers, community health workers, health education specialists, or social and human service assistants, nor does it expand case and support duties to the point of replacing clinical diagnosis, treatment, medication, or judicial decisions.

O*NET and BLS profile highlights | This page corresponds to the exact occupation O*NET/SOC 21-1022.00 "Healthcare Social Workers" (Healthcare Social Workers). Official scope text: Provide individuals, families, and groups with the psychosocial support needed to cope with chronic, acute, or terminal illnesses. Services include advising family caregivers. Provide patients with information and counseling, and make referrals for other services. May also provide case and care management or interventions designed to promote health, prevent disease, and address barriers to access to healthcare. Common job titles include Clinical Social Worker and Hospice Social Worker and LMSW and Medical Social Worker and Nephrology Social Worker and Oncology Social Worker and Psychosocial Coordinator and Renal Social Worker and Social Work Case Manager and Social Worker. The listed tasks given by O*NET include (currently 18 tasks: 15 Core, 2 Supplemental, 1 New): advocating for clients or patients to resolve crises (94); explaining terminal symptoms and available options to clients to help them make informed decisions (90); collaborating with other professionals to assess patients' medical or physical condition and assess client needs (90); referring patients, clients, or families to community resources to assist their recovery and obtain services such as financial assistance and legal aid and housing and job placement or education (88); using consultation data and social work experience to plan and coordinate care and rehabilitation and follow up (83); monitoring, evaluating, and recording client progress against measurable goals in treatment and care plans (83); identifying environmental barriers that impede clients' or patients' progress through interviews and reviewing medical records (81); providing counseling individually and in groups (79); planning discharge arrangements (77); organizing support groups or providing counseling to family members (77); modifying treatment plans as clients' conditions change (77); supervising and guiding other staff (67); planning and conducting programs (60); developing social policy recommendations or assisting community development (54); conducting social research (50); investigating child abuse or neglect cases and taking authorized protective action (88); and overseeing Medicaid and Medicare related documentation and record work in hospitals (63). The highest work activity importance scores are Assisting and Caring for Others (93), Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships (88), Getting Information (87), Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates (86), and Communicating with People Outside the Organization (83). Wage and employment scope note for this page: the U.S. wage and employment and industry data presented by O*NET on the 21-1022.00 page are not marked as taken from a parent occupation; this page adopts them faithfully and labels them in each section as this occupation's (21-1022.00) own scope without substituting values from adjacent occupations. It should also be noted that the page shows a projected 2025—2035 growth of "Much faster than average (7% or higher)" (much faster than average) with a Bright Outlook marker, and O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above), and the education section shows 70% master's degree, 15% bachelor's degree, and 11% post-master's certificate. Currently added task | Conduct psychological assessment of clients is marked New, with no importance provided; task registration does not automatically confer psychological or clinical practice authority.

Standards and quality boundaries | This page involves three types of requirements: first, professional and quality, meaning psychosocial assessment and case and care and referral work must be carried out in accordance with social work professional ethics and institutional standards, with case and referral and progress and cost records kept; second, ethics and privacy and confidentiality, meaning case and counseling and support work must follow confidentiality and informed consent and confidentiality exceptions and professional ethics, and service recipients' and families' sensitive information and health information must be managed in accordance with institutional and legal requirements, and clinical diagnosis or treatment or medication advice must not be provided beyond boundaries; third, records and information, meaning case and progress and referral and cost records must be truthful, complete, and traceable, and materials that are controlled or involve sensitive information and externally disclosed information must be managed according to approval and the minimum necessary principle. This page provides general guidance only and does not constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, psychological, or legal advice.

Recording and collaboration | Record, in accordance with institutional case and ethics and data management policies, the referral and needs and risk identification, psychosocial assessment and care planning, intervention and counseling and support, referral and resource linkage and coordination, progress and outcomes and costs and review, and confidentiality and consent and information disclosure and original records and revision audit trails, and complete them using the prescribed templates and time limits; upon finding safety risks or suspected abuse or neglect or a confidentiality exception or inconsistency between records and the actual situation, pause immediately, report according to authorization, and ask superiors and clinical and ethics and compliance positions to review, and do not modify records without authorization or make retrospective entries.

Boundary conclusion | This page corresponds to O*NET 21-1022.00 (Healthcare Social Workers), and the core difference from adjacent positions lies in "subject matter, output, and authorization level": this occupation takes psychosocial support and case and care and referral for patients and families as its subject matter, and its output is psychosocial assessment and case and care and referral and progress and cost records; Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers (21-1023.00) take mental health and substance abuse treatment as their subject matter; Child, Family, and School Social Workers (21-1021.00) take child and family and school settings as their subject matter; Community Health Workers (21-1094.00) take community health promotion and navigation as their subject matter; Health Education Specialists (21-1091.00) take population health education and promotion programs as their subject matter; and Social and Human Service Assistants (21-1093.00) take providing social service support under professional supervision as their subject matter. Subject matter, output, and authorization level all differ, and the authority for clinical diagnosis, treatment, medication, placement and protection decisions, and judicial decisions cannot be carried over across positions.

Core concept of adjacent positions | Positions in the same group and adjacent positions mostly aim to "bring cases or services or programs to the prescribed state within social work ethics and confidentiality and authorization boundaries and leave an audit trail," differing in subject matter, output, and authorization level: some take psychosocial support and case and care for patients and families as their subject matter, some take mental health and substance abuse treatment or child and family settings or community health promotion or population health education programs as theirs, and some take providing social service support under professional supervision as theirs.

Core purpose of this occupation | Taking patient and family circumstances and medical and social resources as its subject matter, complete the work within social work ethics and confidentiality and authorization: referral and needs and risk identification, psychosocial assessment and care planning, intervention and counseling and support, referral and resource linkage and coordination, progress monitoring and recording and review, and discharge or case closure and handover and follow-up, so that service recipients' needs are addressed, intervention and records are traceable, sensitive information security is controlled, and responsibility boundaries can be explained.

Main subject matter and basis of adjacent positions | Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers rely on mental health and substance abuse treatment and service standards; Child, Family, and School Social Workers rely on child protection and family and school social work standards; Community Health Workers rely on public health and community health promotion standards; Health Education Specialists rely on public health and health education standards; and Social and Human Service Assistants rely on the standards for social service organizations providing support under professional supervision.

Main subject matter and basis of this occupation | The subject matter is disease diagnosis and prognosis and treatment plan, family caregiving resources and financial situation, needs such as housing and legal aid and employment, psychosocial assessment and care and referral, and materials and service recipients' and families' sensitive information and health information, based on social work professional ethics and medical and assistance and mental health and minor protection and older person rights protection standards and institutional case and ethics and data policies.

Occupational profile | The Healthcare Social Workers on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 21-1022.00 (Healthcare Social Workers), which in hospitals and hospice and kidney and oncology and community health and rehabilitation settings carries out psychosocial support and case and care and referral work for patients and families: advocating for clients or patients to resolve crises, assessing needs and planning and coordinating care, providing counseling and organizing support groups, referring to community resources and helping obtain financial and legal and housing and employment services, monitoring and recording progress, and planning discharge and follow-up. Common job titles include Clinical Social Worker and Hospice Social Worker and LMSW and Medical Social Worker and Nephrology Social Worker and Oncology Social Worker and Psychosocial Coordinator and Renal Social Worker and Social Work Case Manager and Social Worker; on the 21-1022.00 page, O*NET shows that the main industry for this occupation in the United States is healthcare and social assistance. The work has Assisting and Caring for Others (importance 93), Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships (88), Getting Information (87), Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates (86), and Communicating with People Outside the Organization (83) as the highest activities, accompanied by telephone conversations 100% every day and face-to-face discussions 96% every day and electronic mail 93% every day and constant contact with others 85%; exposure to disease or infections 41% every day; conflict situations 19% every day and 59% once a week or more; and consequence of error 11% extremely serious and 37% serious. O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above); the education section shows 70% master's degree, 15% bachelor's degree, and 11% post-master's certificate. The U.S. wages and employment presented by O*NET on the 21-1022.00 page follow this occupation's own scope (2025 median hourly wage $32.63 and median annual wage $67,880, 2025 employment 194,800, projected growth of 7% or higher for 2025—2035, and about 16,900 average annual openings during the period).

Core processes of adjacent positions | Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers focus on mental health and substance abuse assessment and treatment and services; Child, Family, and School Social Workers focus on child protection and family and school setting services; Community Health Workers focus on community health promotion and resource navigation; Health Education Specialists focus on designing and evaluating population health education programs; and Social and Human Service Assistants focus on providing social service support under professional supervision.

Core processes of this occupation | Referral and needs and risk identification, psychosocial assessment and care planning, intervention and counseling and support, referral and resource linkage and coordination, progress monitoring and recording and review, and discharge or case closure and handover and follow-up; every step must leave an audit trail in accordance with social work ethics and confidentiality and data policies and must be reviewable by superiors and by clinical and ethics and compliance positions.

Main outputs of adjacent positions | Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers produce mental health and substance abuse assessment and treatment and service records; Child, Family, and School Social Workers produce child protection and family and school service records; Community Health Workers produce community health promotion and resource navigation records; Health Education Specialists produce needs assessments and program plans and evaluation records; and Social and Human Service Assistants produce social service support and assistance records.

Main outputs of this occupation | Psychosocial assessment and care plans; case and care and referral and progress and cost records; intervention and counseling and support group records; records of referral to community resources and assistance in obtaining them; discharge and follow-up and handover records; and traceable confidentiality and consent and information disclosure and ethics compliance records.

Responsibility holder for adjacent positions | Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the employing institution together with professional ethics and regulatory standards, and the objects of responsibility are mostly service recipients and families and peers and public trust and institutional compliance.

Duty boundaries | Psychosocial support and care coordination and recording are tasks of this occupation; in the United States, clinical social workers holding the applicable state license may diagnose and treat mental, behavioral, and emotional problems, so this occupation cannot be categorically excluded from clinical services. Actual medical medication, judicial, protection, data, and disclosure duties must be verified separately against the individual's qualifications, local systems, and institutional authority.

Authority and approval for adjacent positions | The authority of positions in the same group and adjacent positions comes from institutional authorization together with professional ethics and regulatory standards, and generally does not include the authority to decide on their own conclusions and signatures and releases that exceed their own authorization or scope; matters involving clinical decisions and judicial and protection decisions and major disclosures should be referred to the corresponding position or institution.

Authority and reporting | Daily services are subject to the individual's qualifications and institutional authority. The reporting subject, trigger conditions, time limits, and recipients for suspected abuse, violence, or other safety risks are governed by the applicable system; obtaining supervisor approval first must not be written as a precondition for all legally mandated reporting, and this page cannot decide whether a specific case meets the reporting standard.

Boundaries of conclusions for adjacent positions | Conclusions of positions in the same group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to the level of their own project and their own duties, and generally do not constitute a determination of clinical outcomes or diagnosis or legal liability or judicial conclusions; the application of conclusions that cross specialties or involve clinical and judicial and protection matters and major disclosures has its own scope limits.

Boundaries of conclusions | Faithfully distinguish original records, professional judgments, and matters pending confirmation; do not assume services beyond one's own legal qualifications or institutional duties. Real crisis, protection, or disclosure matters are handled by the corresponding personnel under the applicable system; the materials of H01 on this page contain no real risk assessment information and do not judge safety or authorization.

Verification boundaries | U.S. O*NET survey of education requirements for newly hired personnel: master's 70%, bachelor's 15%, post-master's certificate 11%; Zone Five is a description of occupational preparation, not entry requirements in China. Conditions in China should be verified against real positions and local systems, and Beijing's medical social work policy only explains the relationship between its services and the appointment of occupational proficiency certificate holders. The questionnaire and H01 do not constitute hiring, practice, or ability scoring.

Notes on verification points | This occupation focuses on communicating and coordinating with service recipients and families and multiple parties (Assisting and Caring for Others and Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships are the highest activities; telephone conversations 100% every day, face-to-face discussions 96% every day, constant contact with others 85%, working more than 40 hours per week 46%), and emergency and on-call and hospice checkpoints may bring concentrated overtime and emotional pressure; compensation usually consists of base salary plus night and on-call and shortage allowances and performance pay and bonuses, and professional title and post and service field and working hours and allowances and performance criteria must be confirmed in writing.

04 Compensation and working hours and employment contract scope | Verify the composition of the offered compensation (base salary, differences by institution type and service field, night and on-call and emergency and hospice allowances, performance pay and bonuses, training and continuing education and licensure and certification maintenance arrangements), working hours and shift and on-call and emergency arrangements, contract term and full-time or part-time type, probation period and performance criteria (caseload and service quality and ethics compliance and teamwork indicators), and whether service recipients' and families' protected data and health information and position responsibility and professional liability insurance arrangements are involved.

Notes on verification points | The interface relationships with medical and psychological and judicial and assistance and ethics and protection institutions determine the boundaries of cases and placement and protection and data and responsibility and disclosure, and must be clarified in advance.

What kind of personality is better suited to being a Healthcare Social Worker? This occupation values communication and empathy, rigor about ethics and confidentiality and evidence, a sense of responsibility for service recipients' safety and privacy, and stability under crisis and emotional pressure, rather than any particular personality type; the O*NET interest code is SI (Social—Investigative), which can serve as a starting point for exploration.

Are introverts suited to this occupation? Yes. This occupation involves a great deal of case and record and resource organization work, and it also requires communicating with service recipients and families and multiple parties (telephone conversations 100% every day, face-to-face discussions 96% every day, contact with others 85%).

Introversion and extraversion are not a validated occupational threshold here; communication, resource coordination, and recording can be used to observe learning preparation, and the predictive validity of personality versus ethics or skills is not compared.

Which MBTI type is most suitable for this occupation? No type has been proven most suitable. The MBTI is not an occupational qualification or ability assessment tool, and occupational fit depends mainly on case and social work skills and ethics adherence.

Which Holland interest type is more suitable for this occupation? The O*NET interest code is SI: Social (communicating with and supporting and coordinating for people in illness and crisis and their families) and Investigative (understanding cases and social problems with research and evidence and assessment methods); it can be used to explore task preferences, not to predict performance.

This page does not provide validation research on how personality or interests affect performance in this occupation, and no individual work performance conclusions are drawn from questionnaires; real practice also requires verification of qualifications, supervision, and authorization.

Can someone who is not good at math do this occupation? Basic assessment and statistics and research methods and result interpretation abilities are needed; a quantitative foundation can be filled in through training and tool support, but a complete inability to adapt to data and research would be clearly limiting (especially in research and evaluation positions).

Does this occupation require high emotional intelligence? It requires emotional stability and empathy and communication and conflict handling skills, but no specific assessment scores. Crisis and conflict and multi-party communication require self-regulation and communicating and reporting according to procedure.

paragraphs: Boundaries | This page lists the failure types and control points that are relatively common in this occupation's psychosocial assessment and case and care and referral and recording, to help identify and manage risks; it does not constitute any medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, psychological, or legal advice or conclusions about a case; all matters involving clinical judgment, diagnosis and treatment, psychotherapy, placement and protection decisions and judicial processes and external disclosure and the handling of service recipients' and families' sensitive information must be handled by positions or institutions with the corresponding qualifications and by the competent authority in accordance with regulations and ethics and systems. What is described on this page is the general situation of medical social work positions, and the specifics are governed by the Basic Medical and Health Promotion and Mental Health and Minor Protection and Older Person Rights Protection and Personal Information Protection provisions and social work ethics and institutional case policies.

Direct answer | The core risk of this occupation is not whether a case can be followed through, but four types of high-consequence failure: assessment and safety failure (improper crisis assessment or safety response or case and care and referral, or out-of-bounds statements involving clinical diagnosis and treatment and medication or psychotherapy, which may harm service recipients' rights and safety and create institutional reputation and compliance risk), privacy and ethics failure (improper handling of service recipients' or families' sensitive information and health information or case data, or improper informed consent or confidentiality exceptions or mandatory reporting or out-of-bounds sharing, which may cause privacy leaks and ethics and compliance and legal risk), quality and record failure (distorted or version-uncontrolled assessment or progress or referral or cost (medical insurance) records, which may cause unfair services and misjudgment of traceability and performance), and authorization and collaboration failure (making clinical judgments or placement and protection decisions or external disclosures beyond authorization, critical crisis intervention or specialty or referral resource capability resting on a single point, and unclear standards with medical and judicial and ethics and protection institutions on scope and responsibility and disclosure boundaries leading to disputes). O*NET work context shows consequence of error 11% extremely serious and 37% serious, responsibility for others' health and safety 19% extremely high and 26% high, dealing with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people 22% every day and 52% once a week or more, and facing violent or physically aggressive people 15% once a week or more, which are the work context basis for the relatively severe consequences of risk in this occupation.

O*NET supports the task and work context; the six cards are editorial scenarios and do not indicate incidence rates or card-by-card legal determinations. subject.name: Healthcare Social Workers
subject.summary: Healthcare Social Workers provide psychosocial support to individuals, families, and groups coping with acute, chronic, or terminal illness, coordinate care and community resources and service referrals, and record needs and progress. U.S. occupation code 21-1022.00; clinical services and data handling and disclosure authority must be verified against local law, qualifications, and institutional authorization.
